purpose: Make dependency-security results reproducible, auditable, and actionable, including the current transitive yanked bisync finding and advisory exceptions.
scope: Cargo audit/deny configuration and lockfile policy, advisory database update behavior, exception records, and remediation tracking. This is a supply-chain control track, not a license-policy redesign.
non_goals: Promising an immediate upstream replacement for every transitive dependency.
Suppressing a finding merely because it is transitive or development-only.
Adding runtime telemetry or network access to production binaries.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Security CI records the exact cargo-deny/cargo-audit tool version, Cargo.lock digest, and advisory-database Git revision used for each result. Because the audit tool does not natively emit the database revision, the workflow obtains it explicitly with git rev-parse HEAD in the checked-out advisory database and writes it beside the machine-readable report. A maintainer can reproduce a pass or failure from those recorded inputs; database-update/network failures are reported distinctly from a clean audit.

Every active advisory, yanked-package, or license exception has a structured justification naming the affected dependency path, owner or tracking issue, creation date, expiry/review date, and compensating control. An exception expires within at most 90 days of creation; extension requires a new reviewed record explaining why remediation remains blocked. CI fails when an exception expires or its dependency path no longer matches the lockfile.

The current yanked bisync finding on the production dependency path callisto-cli -> callisto-graph is resolved by a compatible dependency update or retained only under an explicit bounded exception meeting AC-002. The release documentation identifies the chosen state; an untracked yanked package cannot remain a silent warning.

The audit command used locally and in CI is documented as one supported task-runner entry point, emits a machine-readable report suitable for artifact retention, and records its reproducibility inputs from AC-001. This track makes no claim about secret redaction because the audit pipeline has no credential input; a future credential-bearing audit integration must add a separately testable logging policy.
